**Direct answer:** GPTQ and AWQ are both post-training, weight-only quantizers for LLMs. They differ in how they limit error. GPTQ compensates rounding error with second-order weight updates. AWQ protects the weights that matter most to the activations by rescaling channels, and it does no weight updates. The reported results don't establish that one is better in general. The papers use different models, bit-widths, baselines and metrics, so the headline numbers aren't comparable. The most direct head-to-head evidence I found is secondary and limited, and I read it only as search-result summaries.

I did this research directly rather than through subagents. Your limits (no shell, no local files, at most eight retrievals) conflicted with the skill's file-writing workflow. I used seven retrievals: one search and six page fetches. Two fetches failed on bad URLs and two returned unparseable PDFs, so those four did not yield usable content.

## Mechanism

- GPTQ is a one-shot weight quantizer based on approximate second-order information. It quantizes 175B-parameter GPT-class models in about four GPU hours and reports 3–4 bit weights with little accuracy loss.
  - https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.17323
- GPTQ builds on Optimal Brain Quantization. It quantizes columns in a fixed order, updates the remaining weights in blocks of 128, and uses a Cholesky reformulation with 1% diagonal dampening.
  - https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2210.17323
- GPTQ calibrates on 128 random 2048-token segments from C4.
  - https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2210.17323
- AWQ finds salient weight channels from activation statistics, not weight magnitude. It scales those channels up through an equivalent transformation, and the paper derives that this reduces quantization error. It uses no backpropagation or reconstruction and does no mixed-precision storage.
  - https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00978
- AWQ's motivation is that about 0.1–1% of weights are salient. Keeping them in FP16 works but is hard to implement efficiently, so AWQ scales them instead. Scaling too far hurts the other channels; the best result in the paper's ablation is s=2.
  - https://arxiv.org/html/2306.00978

## Scope as reported

- GPTQ's main experiments cover OPT and BLOOM at 3 and 4 bits. Metrics are perplexity on WikiText2, PTB and C4, plus zero-shot LAMBADA, ARC and PIQA.
  - https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2210.17323
- GPTQ also reports 2-bit and ternary results, but with small groups, which adds overhead beyond the nominal bit-width. At group size 128, 2-bit costs about 2.2 bits per weight.
  - https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2210.17323
- AWQ's main tables cover OPT, LLaMA, Llama-2, Mistral and Mixtral, mostly at INT3 and INT4 with group size 128. It also covers vision-language models (OpenFlamingo, VILA) and CodeLlama.
  - https://arxiv.org/html/2306.00978
- AWQ is demonstrated at INT2 only combined with GPTQ. Plain round-to-nearest fails completely at INT2.
  - https://arxiv.org/html/2306.00978
- The AWQ authors present TinyChat as their 4-bit inference system. It uses kernel fusion and platform-aware weight packing, and they claim more than 3× speedup over Hugging Face FP16 on desktop and mobile GPUs.
  - https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00978

## What should not be inferred

- **Do not compare the speedups directly.** GPTQ's 3.25× (A100) and 4.5× (A6000) are for batch-size-1 generation with custom kernels, measured against FP16 on 5 and 8 GPUs. AWQ's "more than 3×" is against Hugging Face FP16 on different hardware.
  - https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2210.17323
  - https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00978
- **Do not read the speedups as faster compute or as results for large batches.** GPTQ's gains come from reduced memory movement in memory-bound matrix-vector products. Activations stay unquantized, and the paper says the method "does not lead to computational reductions." I did not verify AWQ's speedup mechanism beyond the abstract.
  - https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2210.17323
- **Do not take AWQ's robustness-to-calibration result as general proof of GPTQ overfitting.** AWQ's claim is that GPTQ's reconstruction may overfit the calibration set, and the evidence is one setting. In OPT-6.7B at INT3-g128, a mismatched PubMed/Enron calibration split raised AWQ's perplexity by 0.5–0.6 and GPTQ's by 2.3–4.9. AWQ also reports needing 16 calibration sequences against 192 for GPTQ. The result comes from the AWQ authors' own comparison, on one model and bit-width.
  - https://arxiv.org/html/2306.00978
- **Do not assume a perplexity ranking carries over to downstream tasks.** A secondary source reported one 70B model where GPTQ had lower WikiText2 perplexity but AWQ scored higher on several benchmarks. Another benchmark reported AWQ-Marlin and GPTQ at perplexity 6.84 and 6.90 but HumanEval Pass@1 of 51.8% and 46.3%, against 56.1% for FP16. I saw these only as a search-result summary of arXiv 2608.30076, not the paper itself, so treat them as unverified.
  - https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.30076
- **Do not treat blog rankings as established.** Several blog and vendor comparisons say AWQ is usually slightly better and quicker to quantize. They are not peer-reviewed, and some of their numbers look approximate. I did not read them in full.
  - https://www.index.dev/skill-vs-skill/ai-gptq-vs-awq-vs-gguf
  - https://gingerlabs.ai/blog/awq-vs-gptq-benchmarks
- **Do not read the 2-bit and low-bit results across methods.** AWQ's INT2 result is only on top of GPTQ. A secondary summary reported GPTQ at 2-bit g128 reaching perplexity 375 on Gemma-1 7B, against 10.4 for FP16. That is one model, taken from a paper about a different method (CDQuant).
  - https://arxiv.org/html/2306.00978
  - https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.17542
- **Do not assume the results cover other things.** GPTQ's paper does not quantize activations and says its effects on secondary measures such as bias were not studied. I found no evidence in these sources on long-context, multilingual or safety behavior. A 2026 study of calibration-language diversity cites both methods, but I couldn't read its body, so I draw no conclusion from it.
  - https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2210.17323
  - https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.18306

## Gaps

- I did not obtain a controlled, peer-reviewed, apples-to-apples GPTQ-versus-AWQ comparison, so "which is better" is unresolved.
- The AWQ evidence comes from the HTML summary of the paper, not the full tables. I didn't see its exact numbers for the main results.
